This study investigated whether an episode of acute malaria in young children results in changes in the peripheral B cell phenotype. METHODS Using flow-cytofluorimetric analysis, the B cell phenotypes found in the peripheral blood of children aged 2-5 years were characterized during an episode of acute uncomplicated clinical malaria and four weeks post-recovery and in healthy age-matched controls.
